Pre-statutory Consultation on the Proposed Closure of Kew Riverside Primary School

Dear Mr Dodds,

I am writing as the parent of two children currently at Kew Riverside Primary School — my daughter Jannat, aged 9, and my son Haris, aged 7. Both children are in Ash class, and both began their entire education at Kew Riverside. I want to share why I believe this school is irreplaceable for our family and urge the council to reconsider this proposal.

A few years ago, we made the decision to move our children to Kings School. It was a short-lived experiment. Within weeks, both Jannat and Haris were asking us, repeatedly and earnestly, to move them back to Kew Riverside. They spoke constantly about how much better cared for they felt there, about the warmth of the teachers, and about the quality of everything the school offered — academically and pastorally. Not a single day went by without them mentioning how much they missed it. We listened to them, and within a month we moved them back. That decision has never been anything but the right one.

I raise this not simply as a fond anecdote, but because it speaks directly to something a budget spreadsheet cannot capture: the quality of care and the sense of safety and belonging that Kew Riverside provides to its pupils. My own children — at ages seven and nine — recognised and articulated this themselves, without prompting, when given a point of comparison. That is a rare and telling thing.

I understand the financial pressures facing the local authority are real, and I do not dismiss them. But I believe strongly that a child's safety, wellbeing, and the quality of their education must be the primary consideration in any decision of this magnitude — not a secondary one weighed against a budget deficit. Kew Riverside's recent Ofsted inspection recognised exactly these qualities: a highly inclusive school, strong relationships with families, high expectations for every pupil, and children who are happy, confident and safe. These are not easy things to build, and they are not easily replaced by reassigning children to a different school with guaranteed places.

I therefore ask the council to:

1. Give genuine weight to the lived experience of families like mine, who have direct, comparative evidence of the difference Kew Riverside makes to a child's education and wellbeing.

2. Explore every alternative to closure — including collaboration, federation, or restructuring — before proceeding further.

3. Recognise that displacing settled, thriving children carries real emotional and educational costs that are difficult to quantify but are no less significant than financial ones.

Kew Riverside changed my children's experience of school for the better, and they told us so in their own words. I urge the local authority to weigh that as heavily as it weighs the numbers on a page.

Yours sincerely,

Samiulhaq

Parent of Jannat and Haris, Ash Class, Kew Riverside Primary School

Kew Riverside Made Kew Feel Like Home

We moved to Kew around 18 months ago, new not only to the area but to the UK. Everything was new to us, and Kew Riverside was one of the first places that truly opened its doors and made us feel welcome.

My son Uzay is now 9 years old. Kew Riverside helped him settle incredibly quickly into a new country and a completely new life. He found friends, confidence and a real sense of belonging. And through him and the school, we found our community too. In many ways, Kew Riverside helped turn Kew from the place we had moved to into our home.

What has touched me most is how every child is seen as an individual. I have watched children with very different needs being genuinely included, supported and given the opportunity to thrive. There is a warmth and sense of belonging here that is difficult to describe until you experience it yourself.

A school like Kew Riverside is much more than a building or its pupil numbers. It is friendships, relationships, trust and a community that has been built over many years.

Uzay loves his school. He feels safe, known and happy there. And there are younger children who deserve the opportunity to grow up with that same experience.

You can close a building on a particular date, but you cannot simply recreate the community that lived inside it.

For our family, Kew Riverside made Kew feel like home. I sincerely hope it will continue to do the same for many more children and families in the years ahead.

Seda Akyürek
Kew Riverside parent
